runs.interaction_thesis:
Tapping a slack row grows that row's own card into the full tide detail.
- The card's clip opens from the row's frame to the whole screen.
- The row's three lines (time, turn, next current) move to their places in the detail header, and the time scales up to the 56 pt hero.
- All of it runs on one `spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0)`, which never overshoots: slack water is the moment the current stands still.
- The rest of the detail fades in after the card has mostly grown (0.2 s ease-out, 0.15 s delay) and fades out first when closing (0.12 s ease-in).
- Dragging the header down collapses the card back into its row.

runs.interaction_thesis: Tapping a slack row grows that row, in place, into the tide detail as one surface on a critically damped spring (`.spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0)`, since slack water does not overshoot). The slack time is the still point: it moves from the row to the head of the detail and never fades. The rest of the detail fades in and rises 12 pt over the second half of the travel. Dragging the head down, or swiping in from the leading edge, shrinks the surface back into its row under the finger. With Reduce Motion on, the finished detail crossfades in over 200 ms instead. Leaving the push loses the edge-swipe back, the bar and its back button, the VoiceOver escape gesture and the navigation path. A leading-edge swipe, a close button and `.accessibilityAction(.escape)` replace the first three; nothing replaces the path, which the app does not restore or deep-link today.

runs.interaction_thesis: Tapping a slack row in the Today list grows that row into its tide detail with the system zoom navigation transition (`.matchedTransitionSource` on the row, `.navigationTransition(.zoom)` on the detail, one shared `@Namespace` keyed by `slack.id`). The detail reads as the row opened up, not as a new page sliding in, and swiping down or back collapses it into the same row, interactively. As the detail arrives, the day's tide line draws left to right through the slack marker with `.smooth(duration: 0.45)`, no delay. With Reduce Motion, the system's own handling replaces the zoom and the line is shown already drawn.
